question: What is the empirically fitted relationship between the rate of change of money, wage, and rate of unemployment known as?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Philips curve**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Philips curve represents the inverse relationship between the rate of unemployment and the rate of inflation in an economy.
 
• The concept was first introduced by economist A.W. Phillips in 1958.
 
• According to the Phillips curve, lower unemployment in an economy leads to higher wages, which in turn leads to higher inflation.
 
• This relationship suggests that policymakers face a trade-off between reducing unemployment and controlling inflation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Friedman's Model**

 
 
• Also known as the Monetarist Theory, it was proposed by Milton Friedman.
 
• Friedman argued that there is no long-run trade-off between inflation and unemployment, as suggested by the Phillips curve.
 
• He introduced the concept of the Natural Rate of Unemployment, which posits that the economy will always revert to this natural rate despite short-term fluctuations.
 
• Friedman emphasized the role of monetary policy in controlling inflation.
 
 
 
• **Keynesian Model**
 
 
• Developed by John Maynard Keynes, this model emphasizes total spending in the economy (aggregate demand) and its effects on output and inflation.
 
• Keynesians advocate for active government intervention to manage economic cycles.
 
• They believe that insufficient demand can lead to prolonged periods of high unemployment.
 
• In contrast to the Phillips curve, Keynesians may support policies that increase aggregate demand to reduce unemployment without necessarily causing high inflation.
 
 
 
• **Baumol Hypothesis**
 
 
• Proposed by economist William J. Baumol, it addresses the cost disease in service sectors.
 
• Baumol's hypothesis suggests that wages in labor-intensive sectors (like services) rise due to wage increases in other sectors that experience higher productivity growth.
 
• This leads to higher costs in the service sector without corresponding increases in productivity.
 
• The hypothesis is often used to explain rising costs in sectors such as healthcare and education.
